{{< pagebreak >}}

Disciplines are the signature mechanic of *Heroes of Legend.* They're how the game knows what your hero has mastered. Not just skills, *domains of power.* Fire. Blades. Protection. The forces and forms your character has attuned to through training, study, or sheer stubborn repetition.

Here's the important part: **Disciplines are prerequisites, not rolls.** You don't roll your Fire Discipline. You don't add your Blades Discipline to an attack. Disciplines are the gate, you need them to *unlock* skills, abilities, and talents. Once you've got them, they represent permanent mastery. No expiration. No forgetting.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## What Are Disciplines?

A Discipline represents a domain of expertise or power your hero has internalized. It's the difference between "I picked up a sword once" and "I've trained with blades for ten years." Between "I read a book about fire" and "Fire answers when I call."

**Example:** A warrior with 3 Blade Disciplines has spent years mastering swords, every angle, every grip, every weakness in every guard. A mage with 3 Fire Disciplines doesn't just cast flames, they *understand* flame, the way a shipwright understands wood. A ranger with 2 Animal Disciplines has bonded with the wild in ways city-folk will never comprehend.

You don't roll Disciplines. You *collect* them. They're permanent markers on your character sheet that say: "I've earned this."

{{< pagebreak >}}

## The Discipline Taxonomy

| Category | Discipline | Represents |
|----------|-----------|------------|
| **Elemental** | **Fire** | Flame, heat, passion, destruction |
| | **Earth** | Stone, stability, endurance, crafting |
| | **Wind** | Air, speed, storms, precision |
| | **Water** | Ice, flow, healing, adaptation |
| **Weapon** | **Blades** | Swords, daggers, finesse and precision |
| | **Axes** | Axes, cleavers, brutal chopping power |
| | **Polearms** | Spears, halberds, reach and control |
| | **Archery** | Bows, crossbows, ranged precision |
| | **Heavy Weapon** | Greatswords, greataxes, mauls, two-handed power |
| | **Unarmed** | Fists, gauntlets, grappling, close-quarters combat |
| **Defense** | **Protection** | Shields, warding, guarding allies |
| | **Armor** | Heavy armor proficiency, damage soaking |
| **Primal** | **Animal** | Beasts, nature, shapeshifting, instinct |
| | **Plants** | Flora, growth, thorns, verdant magic |
| **Arcane** | **Energy** | Raw magical force, metamagic, spellcraft |
| **Divine** | **Life** | Healing, vitality, living things |
| | **Religion** | Faith, blessings, holy power |
| **Esoteric** | **Mind** | Psionics, illusions, mental influence |
| | **Summon** | Calling, binding, conjuring creatures |
| **Subterfuge** | **Stealth** | Hiding, moving unseen, ambush, silence |
| | **Sleight** | Locks, traps, pockets, delicate theft |
| **Knowledge** | **Lore** | Scholarship, history, arcana, ancient secrets |
| | **Tactics** | Strategy, command, reading the battlefield |

Twenty-three Disciplines. Nine categories. Your hero's path through them defines everything they can do.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Acquiring Disciplines

### Starting Disciplines

Your starting Disciplines come from your ancestry (1), your culture (2), and your class (see the Class Disciplines table below).

### Class Disciplines

Your class hands you specific Disciplines at creation. These are your foundation, what your training, tradition, or sheer talent has already taught you:

| Class | Starting Disciplines |
|-------|---------------------|
| Protector | 1 any Weapon + 1 Armor |
| Blade | 1 Blades + 1 Stealth |
| Arcanist | 1 Fire + 1 Energy |
| Shepherd | 1 Protection + 1 Animal |
| Intellect | 1 Lore + 1 any |
| Odd | 2 of any type, different categories |
| Leader | 1 Tactics + 1 Protection |
| Unbalanced | 1 Fire + 1 Water (or Earth/Wind) |
| Shadow | 1 Stealth + 1 Sleight |

Starting disciplines are always rank 1 in distinct disciplines. You may not spend both picks on the same discipline to start with rank 2. Depth comes from progression picks at levels 3, 6, and 9.

### Progression

At levels 3, 6, and 9, you gain one additional Discipline of your choice. Class-favored Disciplines, the ones your class gave you at creation, are always available. Cross-class Disciplines may require narrative justification or story events. Want your Blade to pick up Fire? Make it a story. Find a mentor. Touch a primordial flame. Earn it.

### Magic Items

Rare magic items may grant temporary or permanent Disciplines while attuned or wielded. A *Sword of the Phoenix* might grant +1 Fire Discipline in your hands. Set it down, lose the power. These items are treasures, and the DA should make you work for them.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Disciplines as Prerequisites

Skills, abilities, and talents require specific Disciplines before you can learn them. No Disciplines, no purchase. It's that simple.

| Skill/Ability | Disciplines Required | Tier |
|--------------|---------------------|------|
| Longsword | 1 Blades, 1 Heavy Weapon | Adept |
| Dagger | 1 Blades | Novice |
| Greataxe | 2 Axes | Adept |
| Fireball | 2 Fire | Adept |
| Volcanic Eruption | 2 Fire, 1 Earth | Master |
| Chain Mail | 1 Armor | Novice |
| Shield Block | 1 Protection | Novice |
| Animal Companion | 2 Animal | Adept |
| Magic Missile | 1 Energy | Novice |
| Counterspell | 2 Energy | Adept |

## The Discipline Ladder

Every card (spell, ability, skill) follows a three-tier ladder. The higher you climb, the more Disciplines you need, the bigger the payoff. The tier of a card equals the number of Disciplines it requires as prerequisites: Novice = 1, Adept = 2, Master = 3.

### Card Costs (Flat)

Cards cost Development Points at a flat rate regardless of class:

| Tier | Card DP Cost | Discipline Prerequisites | Level Gate |
|------|-------------|------------------------|------------|
| **Novice** | 2 DP | 1 rank in any one Discipline | None (Level 1) |
| **Adept** | 4 DP | 2 Discipline ranks (see shapes below) | Level 3 |
| **Master** | 8 DP | 3 Discipline ranks (see shapes below) | Level 7 |

### Discipline Rank Costs (Per Class)

Each class pays a different price for each Discipline rank depending on how aligned that discipline is with the class's identity. See @sec-chapter-classes for each class's Discipline cost table. The four cost structures are:

| Cost Structure | Rank 1 | Rank 2 | Rank 3 | Meaning |
|---------------|--------|--------|--------|---------|
| **Home** | 1 DP | 2 DP | 4 DP | Favored — core to the class identity |
| **Adjacent** | 2 DP | 4 DP | 8 DP | Related but not core |
| **Foreign** | 3 DP | 6 DP | 12 DP | Unrelated to the class |
| **Opposed** | 4 DP | 8 DP | 16 DP | Out of class — antithetical to the class |

### Total Cost of a Card

The total cost of a card = its flat card DP cost + the sum of the discipline rank costs from your class's structure for each required discipline.

### Prereq Shapes

The number of disciplines required is fixed by tier (1/2/3). The *composition* of those disciplines has shapes:

| Tier | Disciplines Required | Possible Shapes |
|------|---------------------|-----------------|
| **Novice** | 1 | 1 of any discipline |
| **Adept** | 2 | 2 different, or 2 ranks in the same discipline |
| **Master** | 3 | 3 different, or 2 same + 1 different, or 3 same |

A card requiring 1 Fire is Novice. A card requiring 2 Fire is Adept. A card requiring 3 Fire is Master. A card requiring 2 Fire + 1 Earth is Master (total 3 ranks). A hero's maximum in any single discipline is 3 ranks.

### No-Prereq Basics

Some basic Novice cards (cantrips, basic utility skills) have **no Discipline requirement** and cost only the flat card price (2 DP). These represent minor talents anyone can pick up — a spark of flame too small to harm, a knack for reading a room, a trick of sleight of hand. Adept and Master cards **always** require Disciplines. There are no shortcuts to real power.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Damage Budget {#sec-damage-budget}

Every damaging spell, ability, and maneuver in *Heroes of Legend* is built on a single table. This is the balance spine. Spells are the guide; everything else keys off them.

| Tier | Discipline Requirement | Damage (Weak / Standard / Strong) |
|------|------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Novice** | 1 Discipline | 2 / 4 / 6 |
| **Adept** | 2 Disciplines | 6 / 9 / 12 |
| **Master** | 3 Disciplines | 9 / 15 / 21 |

::: {.callout-note}
## How to Read the Budget

There is no damage roll. The outcome of your attack or casting roll — Weak, Standard, or Strong — determines your damage from the budget table. The hit roll is the damage roll.

The numbers are flat damage points. A Novice Firebolt deals 2 damage on a Weak result, 4 on Standard, 6 on Strong. An Adept Fireball deals 6/9/12. A Master Volcanic Eruption deals 9/15/21. These are flat numbers — no dice. If your homebrew spell or ability doesn't match this table, it's either too weak or too strong. The table is the law. The table is the balance.

See @sec-chapter-arcane-spells and @sec-chapter-divine-spells for the full spell lists. See @sec-chapter-classes for class abilities keyed to this budget.
:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Worked Example: Building a Fire Mage

Kael wants to burn the world. He's an Arcanist — his class gives him 1 Fire and 1 Energy at creation. His ancestry and culture grant additional Disciplines as well.

**Novice (Firebolt):** Requires 1 Fire. Kael has 1 Fire. He qualifies immediately. Firebolt costs 2 DP (flat card cost), and his Arcanist home cost for Fire rank 1 was already paid at creation. Firebolt is his on day one.

**Adept (Fireball):** Requires 2 Fire. Kael has 1 Fire, so he needs one more. At level 3 he takes Fire (now 2 Fire) and buys Fireball the moment the Adept gate opens. Most casters need several levels to reach Adept. Arcanists walk a shorter path to the flame.

**Master (Volcanic Eruption):** Requires 2 Fire + 1 Earth. Kael has 2 Fire and 1 Energy after level 3, so he needs Earth. At level 6 he takes Earth (now 2 Fire, 1 Earth, 1 Energy). When the Master tier unlocks at level 7, he qualifies for Volcanic Eruption. He could branch into Protection for defense, Animal for a familiar, or continue deepening his elemental mastery.

Seven levels to master volcanic fury. Disciplines got him to Master. No shortcuts. No wildcards. Just the path, walked one step at a time.

That's the Discipline system working as intended. Master spells should be achievable before your campaign's climax, but they should still mean something when you cast them. A level 7 Volcanic Eruption says "I built for this." When Kael calls down the mountain's fury, everyone at the table knows he paid for it.
